newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says yen/dlr rate of 110 to 120 appropriate.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says yen/dlr rate of 110 to 120 appropriate.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp executive vice president Akihiro Wada said on Wednesday that a yen/dollar rate of 110 to 120 yen was appropriate for Toyota.

"A yen/dollar rate of 110 to 120, or today's rate of 115 yen is the best rate (for the company). We can make a profit at such a rate. I don't know exactly about currency matters because I'm not in charge of accounting, but it's very difficult (to maker a profit) at a rate of around 90 yen," he told Reuters in an interview.
Asked about speculation by industry analysts that Toyota had made plans to cope with a rate of 90 yen to the dollar, Wada said:
"We have never said before that we made a structure to cope with a yen/dollar rate of 90 yen. Such a rate would be likely to have little impact on products make locally abroad.
"But we would not be able to sell yen-denominated exports to the Middle East and Southeast Asia and other areas at such a rate."
